title: Linkability of repeated telemetry submissions from the same wearer
description: Continuous heart-rate, step-count, GPS, and timestamp data sent from the wearer to the wearable device can be linked across time to the same individual or device profile, enabling reconstruction of routines and persistent tracking.
assumptions: The device stores or processes telemetry under a stable device identifier, account, or otherwise consistent context across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for linkability may vary by catalog version.

title: Identifiability of the wearer from telemetry
description: The combination of GPS traces, timestamps, activity patterns, and physiological telemetry can uniquely identify the wearer, even if explicit identifiers are absent.
assumptions: Telemetry is sufficiently granular and retained long enough for correlation with external knowledge such as home/work locations or known routines.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for identifiability may vary by catalog version.

title: Detectability of sensitive states or presence from captured signals
description: The mere presence and timing of telemetry updates, especially GPS and heart-rate measurements, may reveal that the wearer is present at a location, exercising, sleeping, or experiencing notable physiological changes.
assumptions: An observer or internal component can access metadata or infer state from the existence, timing, or coarse values of the transmitted data.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for detectability may vary by catalog version.

title: Disclosure of highly sensitive personal data to the device
description: This flow includes health-related telemetry and precise location history, which are sensitive personal data. If the device or its software exposes, stores, or forwards them insecurely, the wearer’s private information may be disclosed.
assumptions: The device persists, displays, transmits onward, or otherwise makes telemetry accessible beyond the minimum necessary local sensing path.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for disclosure of information may vary by catalog version.

title: Unawareness of continuous and granular sensing
description: The wearer may be unaware of the full extent, frequency, precision, or sensitivity of telemetry captured continuously by the device, including how GPS and timestamps enable inference of habits and locations.
assumptions: Not all sensing details, defaults, or implications are clearly communicated at the time of collection.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for unawareness may vary by catalog version.

title: Non-compliance risk from excessive or unjustified collection
description: Continuous collection of heart rate, steps, GPS position, and timestamps may exceed what is necessary for a given purpose or lack a valid legal basis, creating risk of violating data minimization, purpose limitation, transparency, or consent requirements.
assumptions: The system collects all listed telemetry by default or without sufficiently specific purpose, notice, consent, or configurable controls.
uncertainty_note: Best-effort node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree for non-compliance may vary by catalog version.

title: Linkability of repeated sync batches via persistent device identifier
description: The wearable sends a stable device identifier together with exercise sessions, GPS traces, and timestamps. This can allow the companion app, or parties with access to app-side data, to link multiple uploads over time to the same device and build a longitudinal activity profile.
assumptions: The device identifier is stable across syncs and visible to the receiving app or its storage/telemetry components.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may vary depending on whether persistent identifiers are modeled under linkability of messages or identifiers.

title: Identifiability of the wearer from device ID and detailed activity data
description: Device ID, precise GPS traces, exercise sessions, and timestamps can directly or indirectly identify the individual wearer. Home/work locations and routine patterns inferred from GPS and time data can make the person identifiable even if explicit account data is absent in this flow.
assumptions: The companion app can access raw GPS traces and timestamps and may associate them with a user account or other local identifiers.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best estimate for identifiability from direct and quasi-identifiers in received data.

title: Disclosure of sensitive personal activity and location data in transit or at receipt
description: The sync contains sensitive personal data, including health/activity information, location traces, timestamps, and device identifier. If the transfer channel or app-side handling is insufficiently protected, unauthorized parties could access intimate behavioral and location details.
assumptions: Threat applies if transport security, local app protections, or logging practices are weak or misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for information disclosure on a data flow; exact subtree may differ based on whether disclosure is modeled in transit, endpoint exposure, or logging.

title: Detectability of user activity and sync events from observable transfer patterns
description: Even without reading payload contents, the occurrence, timing, size, or frequency of syncs from the wearable to the app may reveal when the user exercised, traveled, or used the device. Observers of the device-app interaction could detect sensitive events from metadata alone.
assumptions: An attacker can observe local wireless traffic, app notifications, or system-level transfer metadata.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; detectability trees often distinguish existence of communication from detectability of specific sensitive events.

title: Unawareness of collection granularity and inference potential
description: Users may not realize that syncing exercise sessions together with precise GPS traces, timestamps, and device ID enables detailed inference about routines, home/work locations, health patterns, and long-term behavior. The privacy impact of the sync may therefore not be transparent to them.
assumptions: The app does not clearly explain the categories, precision, retention, and inference potential of synced data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for insufficient user awareness/transparency; exact subtree may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Non-compliance risk from collecting more precise data than necessary
description: Syncing precise GPS traces, timestamps, and persistent device identifiers may exceed what is necessary for core companion-app functionality if less granular or less persistent data would suffice. This creates risk of violating data minimization, purpose limitation, retention, or consent requirements.
assumptions: Applicable where the app's stated purpose does not require full-resolution location history or persistent identifiers for every sync.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate because non-compliance trees vary by legal principle such as minimization, purpose limitation, transparency, or consent.

title: Insufficient evidence of user consent or initiation for sensor-data sync
description: The wearable may automatically transmit sensor batches to the companion app without preserving reliable evidence that the user agreed to this specific collection and transfer behavior. This can lead to disputes about whether the sync was authorized or expected.
assumptions: Sync can occur automatically or by default, and the system lacks auditable records of consent/preferences relevant to this flow.
uncertainty_note: Repudiation-related privacy threats are less central on this flow; node id is a best-effort approximation.

title: Meal and weight logs can be linked to the user's identity/account
description: Calorie intake, meal details, and weight entries are highly personal health-related data. When entered into the companion app under a persistent account or device identifier, the records can be linked to the wearer’s real-world identity or stable profile.
assumptions: The app maintains a persistent user account, device identifier, or profile for storing entries.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for identifiability via direct association with an account/profile; exact LINDDUN Pro node naming may vary.

title: Repeated nutrition and weight entries enable linkability across sessions
description: Multiple manual logs over time can be correlated to the same wearer through account identifiers, device identifiers, timestamps, or behavioral patterns, allowing construction of a longitudinal profile of eating habits and weight changes.
assumptions: Entries are stored with timestamps and associated with the same app instance, account, or device over time.
uncertainty_note: Node id is a best-fit estimate for linkability of records across sessions/time.

title: Sensitive health and lifestyle information is disclosed to the app
description: The user discloses calorie intake, meals, and weight to the companion app. These data reveal health status, diet, routines, and potentially medical conditions or body-image-related information beyond what may be necessary for basic app functionality.
assumptions: The app receives and stores the full content of the user’s manual entries.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for disclosure of sensitive personal content to the receiving process.

title: Detailed meal and weight logs enable inference of sensitive attributes
description: From calorie intake, meal composition, and weight trends, the app or anyone with access to the data may infer sensitive attributes such as dieting behavior, pregnancy, eating disorders, religious practices, chronic illness, or other health conditions.
assumptions: The app retains sufficiently granular entries and metadata to support profiling or inference.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for detectability/inference from content; exact node mapping may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: User may be unable to plausibly deny having entered specific logs
description: If the app keeps authenticated, timestamped records of manual calorie, meal, and weight entries, those records can later be used to assert that the wearer submitted specific information, reducing plausible deniability.
assumptions: The app stores timestamps and ties entries to an authenticated account or device.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-repudiation caused by persistent authenticated logging.

title: Insufficient transparency about collection and downstream use of nutrition and weight data
description: The wearer may not understand what exact fields are collected, how long meal and weight logs are retained, whether they are used for profiling or recommendations, or whether they are shared onward. This undermines user awareness and informed expectations.
assumptions: The app’s interface or notices may not fully explain collection, retention, inference, and sharing practices at the point of entry.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for lack of user awareness/transparency; exact node id may differ.

title: Collection of calorie, meal, and weight data may exceed necessity or valid consent
description: Because these entries are sensitive health-related data, collecting or retaining them without clear necessity, explicit consent where required, purpose limitation, or appropriate minimization may create non-compliance risk under privacy and health-data regulations.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy treats these data as sensitive and imposes heightened requirements for consent, minimization, retention limits, or purpose limitation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id for non-compliance due to over-collection/insufficient legal basis; exact LINDDUN Pro node mapping may vary.

title: Sensitive health logs can be inferred from stored records
description: The health log store contains detailed calorie intake, weight history, and exercise session records. Access to these records, or even derived metadata from them, can reveal sensitive health conditions, lifestyle patterns, dieting behavior, pregnancy, eating disorders, injuries, or religious/cultural habits.
assumptions: The datastore persists logs with sufficient granularity and retention to support inference of sensitive personal attributes.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro subtree may differ.

title: Health log entries may be linkable across sessions and contexts
description: Repeated writes of health logs tied to the same account, device, or stable identifier can allow records over time to be linked together, building a longitudinal profile of the user's behavior and health-related activities.
assumptions: Records are stored with stable user, device, or account identifiers, or otherwise contain quasi-identifiers enabling correlation.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact LINDDUN Pro node may be more specific to linkability via identifiers or metadata.

title: Behavioral patterns can be inferred from write timing and metadata
description: Even if individual log contents are protected, timestamps, frequency of updates, record sizes, and categories written to the store can reveal routines such as meal times, workout schedules, weight-tracking intensity, or periods of illness or inactivity.
assumptions: The datastore or supporting infrastructure retains observable metadata such as timestamps, event frequency, or category labels.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; this is an inference threat based on metadata rather than direct content exposure.

title: Stored health logs may disclose sensitive personal data to unauthorized parties
description: If access controls, encryption, segregation, or backend handling are insufficient, the written health logs may be exposed to internal staff, other users, third parties, or attackers, revealing intimate health and lifestyle information.
assumptions: The datastore is accessible by multiple components, administrators, or services, and disclosure controls may fail or be misconfigured.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact disclosure subtree may distinguish stored-data disclosure from transfer disclosure.

title: Users may be unaware that detailed health logs are persistently stored
description: The mobile app may not make it sufficiently clear that calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions are written to a backend health log store and retained over time, limiting user awareness of the extent of processing.
assumptions: Notice in the app is incomplete, unclear, or not presented at the point of collection/storage.
uncertainty_note: Node id is approximate; exact LINDDUN Pro node for unawareness may be more specific to lack of transparency about storage/retention.

title: Storage of detailed health logs may exceed consent or legal basis
description: Calorie intake, weight history, and exercise data can qualify as sensitive or health-related personal data in some jurisdictions. Persisting these logs without explicit consent, appropriate legal basis, purpose limitation, or retention controls may violate privacy requirements.
assumptions: Applicable law or policy treats some or all of these logs as regulated personal or health-related data, and governance controls may be insufficient.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; exact non-compliance subtree may vary by legal-basis, consent, retention, or purpose-limitation focus.

title: The app may be unable to prove what health data was written and under whose action
description: If the write operation lacks adequate auditability, the system may not be able to demonstrate whether a specific health log entry was submitted by the user, generated automatically, modified before storage, or written under a particular account context. This can undermine accountability and dispute resolution.
assumptions: Write operations are not strongly logged with integrity protection, actor context, and timestamps.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node id from memory; repudiation coverage in LINDDUN Pro may be modeled differently for data creation versus transmission.

title: Stored location traces enable linkage of records to the same individual over time
description: GPS traces with timestamps written to the location history store can be linked together to build a persistent mobility profile for one user or device across sessions and contexts. Even if direct identifiers are minimized elsewhere, repeated spatiotemporal patterns make records linkable.
assumptions: The store retains multiple traces per user/device or otherwise preserves a stable association between writes.

title: Location history can identify an individual through unique mobility patterns
description: Fine-grained GPS traces with timestamps are often highly unique and can reveal home, workplace, and habitual routes, allowing identification of the person behind the stored records even without explicit identity fields.
assumptions: Location precision and retention are sufficient to infer recurring sensitive places or unique trajectories.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from quasi-identifying location data; exact node id may differ in the official tree.

title: Location history reveals sensitive activities and habits
description: The stored traces disclose where and when a person has been, enabling inference of visits to sensitive places such as clinics, places of worship, political events, or intimate locations, as well as daily routines and social patterns.
assumptions: The store contains sufficiently granular timestamps and coordinates, and data can be queried or analyzed later.

description: Persistently storing detailed location history expands the amount of personal data available for later access, breach, internal misuse, or secondary analysis, increasing the privacy impact beyond what may be necessary for the app's purpose.

uncertainty_note: Node id is an approximate best fit for disclosure risk driven by over-collection/retention rather than transmission alone.

title: Users may be unaware that precise location history is being stored

uncertainty_note: Best-fit detectability/unawareness node for insufficient user awareness of storage; exact node id may differ.

title: Storing detailed location history may exceed consent or purpose limitations
description: Writing precise GPS traces with timestamps to the location history store may be non-compliant if the retention, granularity, or downstream use is broader than the user's consent, the stated purpose, or applicable data minimization and storage limitation requirements.
assumptions: The app's consent, privacy notice, or legal basis does not clearly cover this level of collection, retention, or use.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-compliance node; exact official node id may vary depending on whether the issue is consent, purpose limitation, or minimization.

description: If the companion app writes location traces without durable records of the user's consent choices or authorization context, it may be difficult to demonstrate that collection and storage were legitimately permitted, enabling repudiation by the user or inability to evidence compliance.
assumptions: Consent or authorization is required for this processing and audit evidence is not reliably captured.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit non-repudiation/privacy-accountability node; exact node id may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Cross-session health logs enable linkage of records to the same individual
description: The analytics service reads calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions from the health log store. Even if individual entries were collected at different times, stable identifiers or consistent account references can allow the service to link multiple records together and build a longitudinal profile of one person.
assumptions: The store exposes a stable user/account identifier, pseudonym, or other persistent key to the analytics service.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best estimate for linkability via persistent identifiers across sessions.

title: Health-condition analysis may identify the individual behind stored logs
description: Combining calorie, weight, and exercise histories for health-condition analysis can make a person identifiable, especially when the analytics service has access to account context or can correlate distinctive behavioral patterns with other data it holds.

description: Reading calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions enables the analytics service to infer sensitive information such as obesity status, eating disorders, pregnancy-related changes, chronic disease indicators, injury recovery, or other health conditions beyond the raw data originally recorded.
assumptions: The service performs profiling or statistical analysis over historical logs.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for detectability/disclosure-by-inference style threat; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

description: The flow provides detailed calorie, weight, and exercise logs across sessions to the analytics service. If full-granularity histories are read when only aggregated trends or a limited time window are needed, the disclosure is excessive and increases privacy risk.
assumptions: The analytics task could be completed with less detailed, aggregated, or shorter-retention data.

title: Users may be unaware that logs are reused for health-condition analysis

This creates a risk that processing is insufficiently transparent or understandable to users.

assumptions: The logs constitute personal and potentially special-category health-related data, and the original collection context did not clearly authorize this analysis.

title: Cross-session location history enables linkage of records to the same individual
description: The analytics query uses location history across sessions, which can link multiple sessions and records together as belonging to one person. Persistent movement traces are highly linkable over time, enabling construction of a unified behavioral profile.
assumptions: Location history records contain a stable user, device, account, or pseudonymous identifier that allows cross-session querying.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is my best fit for linkability via correlating records across sessions; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may vary.

description: Deriving daily routines and movement patterns from historical location data can reveal home/work locations and unique travel habits, making the person identifiable even if direct identifiers are absent.
assumptions: The analytics output or intermediate data preserves sufficiently granular spatiotemporal patterns to single out a person.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for identifiability from quasi-identifying location patterns; exact subnode may differ in LINDDUN Pro.

title: Inference of sensitive habits and lifestyle from movement patterns
description: Analyzing location history across sessions can disclose private information such as home address, workplace, religious attendance, medical visits, political activity, or intimate relationships by inferring patterns from repeated visits and routines.
assumptions: Analytics has access to sufficiently detailed and long-term location history and can correlate visited places with sensitive categories.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for disclosure by inference from observed data; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary.

title: Analytics exceeds user expectations for the original purpose of location collection
description: Using stored location history to derive daily routines and movement patterns may go beyond what users reasonably expect when location data was originally collected, especially if collection was for immediate service functionality rather than behavioral profiling.
assumptions: The original collection context did not clearly communicate cross-session behavioral analytics as a purpose.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for policy/expectation non-compliance or secondary use; exact LINDDUN Pro subnode naming may differ.

title: Users may be unaware of cross-session profiling from stored location history
description: Because the flow queries historical location data to derive routines, users may lack awareness that their movements are retained and analyzed longitudinally, reducing transparency about the existence and extent of profiling.
assumptions: Notices or UI do not clearly explain retention and analytics of location history across sessions.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for lack of awareness/transparency; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may vary.

description: Querying a location history store to derive routine and movement patterns may be incompatible with consent obtained for primary service delivery, and may process more historical data than necessary for the stated purpose.
assumptions: Applicable privacy requirements constrain secondary use, retention, or profiling of precise location data.
uncertainty_note: Best-fit node for non-compliance with consent/purpose limitation/data minimization obligations; exact LINDDUN Pro node id may differ.

uncertainty_note: Best-effort node selection for lack of awareness/transparency; exact subnode may differ in a specific LINDDUN Pro tree.

This can create a mismatch between the disclosed processing purpose and the actual inferred outputs delivered to the app.
